title: On-call & Incident Response Playbook: Process, Runbooks, Rotations, Game Days, and Communication Templates
author: Asha Raman
body:
Summary:
This document codifies Redwood Inference's standard on-call and incident response practices. It includes the incident severity taxonomy, escalation paths, runbook templates, postmortem requirements, on-call rotation guidance, recommended game day exercises, and standardized customer and status page communication templates. Intended audience: SRE, Platform, Serving Runtime, Product, and Support teams.

1. Incident taxonomy and SLO thresholds
- Sev 1 (P0): Total production outage or severe degradation that impacts ~>25% of customer requests, or latency >5x target for >5 minutes, or data loss/security incidents. Target response: pager acknowledged in 5 minutes, mitigation plan in 15 minutes.
- Sev 2 (P1): Partial outage, significant feature degradation impacting a subset of customers or workflows. Target response: pager acknowledged in 15 minutes, mitigation plan in 60 minutes.
- Sev 3 (P2): Functional degradation with workaround, non-urgent customer impact. Response during business hours; owner assignment within 24 hours.
- Sev 4 (P3): Minor issues, documentation/ops tasks, tracked in backlog.

SLOs referenced for escalation:
- API 99.9% availability per region monthly (SRE-owned)
- 95th percentile request latency <= 250ms for short-generation routes
- Error rate alert threshold: error ratio >0.5% sustained for 10 minutes triggers paging for critical routes

2. Pager roles and responsibilities
- Primary on-call: first responder; owns triage and immediate mitigation.
- Secondary/backup: steps in if primary unavailable or escalation required; owns customer comms if primary focused on mitigation.
- Engineering lead (on-call lead): responsible for cross-team escalation and long-running mitigation ownership during the incident.
- Incident commander (IC): appointed for incidents expected to last >2 hours or that require multi-team coordination.
- Communications lead: drafts/status updates and coordinates status page and customer emails.
- Post-incident owner: ensures RCA and action items are tracked and closed.

3. Incident lifecycle (high level)
- Detection: automated alert, customer report, or internal observation.
- Triage (0-15 min): Primary acknowledges pager, assesses severity, and documents initial findings in the incident channel (PagerDuty + Slack #incidents).
- Mitigation (15-60+ min): Apply known runbook steps. If no runbook, gather diagnostics and implement triage mitigation to restore service or reduce impact.
- Escalation: If unresolved within SLA for severity, escalate to secondary/engineering lead/IC per escalation matrix.
- Communication: Issue initial status within 30 minutes on internal channel and status page; provide customer-facing acknowledgement if customer-impacting.
- Resolution: Confirm restored service, monitor for regression for at least 30 minutes, and close incident when stable.
- Postmortem: Postmortem published within 5 business days for Sev1/Sev2; within 10 business days for Sev3 if requested.

4. Runbook template (use for each critical service)
- Title: short service name and primary failure mode
- Owner: oncall rotation and service owner (team and individual)
- Pager signals: specific alerts that should page (alert name, metric, threshold)
- Preconditions: permissions, consoles, runbook links, observable dashboards, runbook test plan
- Step 1: immediate mitigation checklist (commands, API calls, UI steps)
- Step 2: common diagnostics (logs, metrics, traces, KV cache checks, process list, GPU memory, network checks)
- Step 3: rollback or restart steps including safe rollout commands and verification steps
- Step 4: escalation matrix (who to call, contact methods, secondary actions)
- Post-incident actions: follow-up verification, side-effect checks, customer notification follow-up

Runbook example excerpt for model-serving pool OOM: 
- Pager signal: alert:model-serving:oom-rate > 0 for 3 nodes in 5m
- Immediate mitigation: remove new traffic by setting route weight to fallback variant, scale down batch size, cordon affected GPU nodes via autoscaler API: curl -X POST https://infra.internal/api/cordon-node --data '{"node":"gpu-12"}'
- Diagnostics: check dmesg, nvidia-smi, process core dumps at /var/crash, check kernel OOM killer logs
- Escalate to runtime-kernel oncall if kernel-level OOMs continue after mitigation

5. Postmortem requirements and template
- Required for Sev1 and Sev2 incidents. Postmortem must be published as a Confluence page and include:
  - Title and incident ID
  - Summary (what happened, impact by customer/region, duration)
  - Timeline (minute-by-minute condensed timeline of key events)
  - Root cause analysis (technical cause and contributing factors)
  - Corrective actions (short-term mitigations and long-term fixes) with owners and due dates
  - Verification plan and metrics to track
  - Customer communication summary and any follow-up commitments
  - Lessons learned and prevented regressions (playbook improvements, monitoring gaps)

Template fields (to copy into Confluence):
- incident_id: string
- severity: Sev1|Sev2|Sev3
- start_time: ISO8601 string
- end_time: ISO8601 string
- impacted_customers: list of IDs or product areas
- root_cause: short description
- action_items: bullet list with owner and ETA

6. On-call rotations and handoff guidelines
- Rotation cadence: standard weekly rotations for SRE and Platform (Mon 09:00 UTC to next Mon 09:00 UTC). Short rotations (48 hours) allowed for small teams with engineer consent.
- Scheduling: all rotations published in the team calendar and PagerDuty schedule.
- Handoff checklist (to be completed at shift change):
  - Confirm PagerDuty schedule shows correct handoff
  - Review open incidents and ongoing mitigations
  - Verify access to consoles and credentials (vault tokens, KMS access)
  - Note ongoing maintenance windows or deploys that affect SLOs
  - Confirm secondary/backup contact is reachable
- Vacation and escalation: primary must update PagerDuty and Slack statuses; escalate coverage gaps to the rotation manager.

7. Game day exercises
- Purpose: validate runbooks, test tooling, verify escalation, and train responders.
- Recommended cadence: quarterly service-focused game days and an annual cross-team full-stack exercise.
- Example scenarios: control-plane outage, autoscaler failure, model corruption, region network partition, status page pipeline failure.
- Game day conduct:
  1. Pre-announce window and scope to stakeholders (non-customer impacting sandbox)
  2. Inject failure (simulated alert) and start the timer
  3. Observe response, time to page, time to mitigation, and communication cadence
  4. Debrief within 48 hours and publish game day report with improvements and action items

8. Status page and customer communication templates
- Status page entries should be concise and factual, include impact, affected regions/features, mitigation steps, ETA for next update, and resolution. Example status page template:
  - Title: Degraded API performance in us-west-2
  - Impact: Some customers may see increased latency and 5xx errors for text-generation routes in us-west-2 (~18% of traffic).
  - Current status: Investigating
  - Mitigation: Traffic shifted to fallback model; autoscaler scaling policy adjusted
  - Next update: 2026-02-08T15:30Z
  - Reference: internal incident ID INC-2026-0423

- Customer email template (initial acknowledgement):
  Subject: Redwood Inference incident: degraded API performance in us-west-2
  Body:
  Hello,

  We are investigating an issue affecting text-generation latency and errors in the us-west-2 region. Our engineering team has identified increased load on the model-serving pool and are actively mitigating by shifting traffic to a fallback model variant. We will provide an update within 30 minutes.

  If you are experiencing a critical outage, please reply to this message with your account ID and example request IDs.

  Thank you for your patience,
  Redwood Support

- Customer update template (progress):
  Subject: Update: Redwood Inference incident in us-west-2
  Body:
  Hello,

  Update: latency has improved by 70% after the traffic shift and autoscaler adjustments. We continue to monitor and validate. Estimated time to full restoration: 2 hours.

  Impacted customers: list (if known)
  Workaround: re-try or route to alternative region if applicable

  We will send a final resolution email when service is fully restored.

- Customer resolution template:
  Subject: Resolved: Redwood Inference incident in us-west-2
  Body:
  Hello,

  The incident affecting text-generation in us-west-2 is resolved. Root cause: a runaway model training job consuming shared GPU capacity; short-term mitigation included traffic shift and autoscaler tuning. Long-term remediation: isolate training clusters and add autoscaler guardrails (ETA: 2026-04-15).

  We apologize for the disruption and will follow up with a postmortem published at: <link-to-postmortem>.

  Regards,
  Redwood Support

9. Metrics, dashboards, and tooling checklist for responders
- Must-have dashboards: global request rate, error rate by route, latency p50/p95/p99 by route, model-serving pool utilization, GPU memory and temperature, autoscaler queue length, KV cache hit rate.
- CLI tools and access: pagerdutyCTL, infra-api, kubectl context names, model-serving admin UI, logsearch queries (examples included in runbooks).

10. Governance and continuous improvement
- Incident review cadence: weekly postmortem review meeting for the previous week's Sev1/Sev2 incidents.
- Runbook ownership: each critical service runbook has an assigned owner and is reviewed quarterly.
- Game day retros and action tracking: action items created in Jira and linked to the Confluence postmortem.

Related pages and references:
- /confluence/eng-sre/monitoring-standards (monitoring playbook)
- /confluence/eng-platform/oncall-schedules (rotation calendar)
- /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/model-serving-runbook-2026
- Incident postmortem template: /confluence/templates/postmortem-template

Appendix A: Quick escalation matrix (phone + Slack)
- Primary -> Secondary (after 15 minutes)
- Secondary -> Engineering lead (after 60 minutes)
- Engineering lead -> CTO or VP Eng (for prolonged Sev1s or customer-impacting incidents)

Appendix B: Example runbook commands (safe examples)
- cordon node: infractl cordon --node gpu-12
- scale down batcher: curl -X POST https://infra.internal/api/batcher/scale --data '{"service":"model-a","scale":2}'
- route weight change (traffic shift): curl -X PATCH https://routes.internal/api/routes/model-a --data '{"weights":{"fallback":0.9,"primary":0.1}}'

If you are reading this as an on-call responder: bookmark the runbooks referenced above, verify your PagerDuty contact information is current, and complete the handoff checklist at the start of your shift.
